newsitem.title: BELGIUM: French pension plan won't affect EMU - report.
newsitem.headline: French pension plan won't affect EMU - report.

text.p: European Monetary Union (EMU) should not be affected by whether or not France is allowed to use France Telecom pension funds to reduce its public deficit, a market brief by Chase Investment Bank Limited said on Wednesday.
"In practice, EMU is very unlikely to stand or fall on such an issue," the report said. "If it seemed likely to be that important, the politicians would probably ensure that the payment was allowed."

The mark jumped in Europe on Tuesday on talk that an EU financial accounts committee had failed to recommend to the Commission that it accept the French plan to transfer 37.5 billion francs from France Telecom to French government finances.
A spokesman for European Union Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy on Tuesday denied the reports, saying no decision had been made.
The Chase market note said Europe's high yielding bond markets would remain difficult in the abscence of a decision.

At issue is whether the transfer of money to cover future pension liabilities at the state telecoms operator can be used by the French government in its accounting to reduce its public deficit next year to meet the Maastricht treaty criteria for European monetary union.
De Silguy's spokesman said the Commission had received details of what France plans and that it was examining them.

An advisory committee of statistical experts from EU member states had met, he said. "In the light of the result of that discussion and the technical considerations...they (EUROSTAT) will take a decision in the next few days or weeks."
